title: Use the explicit received-pair bound directly for the initial mark

add.label: Conditioned failure bound
add.name: Correct guess and extraction failure under the coupling
add.explain: Condition on the coupled randomness shared by the two message experiments.
add.proof:
For a fixing $C$ of the coins of the coupled run $\mathsf{R}_\$$ with no target query, the conditional probability of $b'=b\land\mathsf{Fail}$ is at most $1/2$ because the output bit is fixed independently of $b$.
For a fixing $C$ with a target query, the same conditional probability is at most $\big(1+\Pr[\mathsf{Fail}\mid C]\big)/2$ by the pointwise bound $\mathbf1_{b'=b\land\mathsf{Fail}}\le (1+\mathbf1_{\mathsf{Fail}})/2$.
Averaging the two bounds over the coupled coins and the uniform bit gives $\Pr[b'=b\land\mathsf{Fail}]\le 1/2+(f_0+f_1)/4$.

add.label: Guessing probability bounds
add.name: Pivot-column conditioning
add.statement: For a stack $\mathbf W$, let $A$ be the matrix obtained by stacking its cells vertically. Then $\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)\le g^{-\operatorname{rank}\mathbf W}$. For every $v$ in its row space, $\operatorname{gp}(v^\top)\ge\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)$.
add.explain: Condition on the nonpivot coordinates of the independent input to the sampler.
add.proof:
Choose a basis of columns indexed by $J$, including column $0$ whenever it is nonzero.
Condition on $r_i$ for $i\in[N]\setminus J$, which fixes the contribution of all columns outside $J$ because column $0$ is zero if excluded.
The independence of the columns indexed by $J$ implies each fixed value of $Ar$ has at most one possible assignment to $r_J$.
The conditional probability of any specified $r_J$ is at most $g^{-|J|}$ by the sampler's independent choices on $[N]$ and its conditional uniformity at $0$.
Averaging gives $\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)\le g^{-|J|}$ since $|J|=\operatorname{rank}\mathbf W$.
For a row-space vector $v$, choose $a$ with $v^\top=a^\top A$.
For each $u$, event inclusion gives $\Pr[Ar=u]\le\Pr[v^\top r=a^\top u]$.
Taking maxima gives $\operatorname{gp}(v^\top)\ge\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)$.

add.label: Ledger interpolation bound
add.name: Security ledger by the quadratic chord gap
add.statement: Under (P5), for every integer $0\le Q<2^\lambda$, $E(2Q+2)\le (Q+1)/2^\lambda$. Write $U=2^\lambda-1$ and $F(x)=E(2x+2)-(x+1)/2^\lambda$.
add.explain: Compute the exact difference between the chord and the quadratic.
add.proof:
The first inequality in (P5) gives $F(0)\le 0$.
Adding the two inequalities in (P5) gives $F(U)\le 0$.
For $0\le t\le1$, expansion gives $F(tU)=(1-t)F(0)+tF(U)-(2\theta+20\varepsilon_f)t(1-t)U^2$.
Bounding the three displayed summands by zero gives $F(Q)\le0$ for $Q\in[0,U]$.

add.label: Charged mark bound
add.name: Charged comparisons from symbolic entries
add.statement: With $u=2Q+2$ in the extraction experiment, the probability of a charged first mark is at most $N_{\mathrm{cmp}}(u)(\theta+\varepsilon_f)+(\binom{L+3u}{2}+L+3u)\varepsilon_f$. Every run reaching its target query has a first mark of type $\mathsf{init}$, $\mathsf{guess}$, charged, or good. Write $\varpi=\Omega_{22}\zeta\zeta'\zeta''\varepsilon$ and $d_f=3D+2n+2K_1+6$.
add.explain: Classify comparison coefficients by their guess-variable degree before applying the grid bound.
add.proof:
Use the coupled run $\mathsf R_\$$ to determine the first mark by the coupling definition.
The symbolic game and the real run agree through the history before the first evaluated collision by the lazy-sampling demand.
No first mark is set before any collision or target query by (M1)–(M4).
A collision of formally unequal received expressions gives $\mathsf{init}$ by (M1).
A good collision cannot have a fresh guessed operand as the later entry, because its uncanceled fresh variable would violate the definition of good.
The later entry of a good noninitial collision is therefore a result.
If a good noninitial collision precedes a target query, (M3) sets a good $\mathsf{diff}$ mark.
If a target query comes first, (M4) sets a guess mark when its label has no entry.
If the label has an entry, the agreeing tables identify that entry as a symbolic key value.
In that case a good key value gives a good $\mathsf{key}$ mark by (M4).
Thus every charged first mark is accounted for by a bad collision or a bad key value in the evaluated symbolic game.
The monitor definition classifies all first marks as $\mathsf{init}$, $\mathsf{guess}$, charged or good.
By (M4), a run reaching the target query has a first mark.

In a fixed symbolic transcript, compare two specified entries or one specified entry with the key.
If the comparison contains guesses, choose a nonconstant guess monomial with formally nonzero coefficient.
The expression rules make this coefficient a nonzero scalar or a formally nonzero source-group expression.
At each fixed $r$, clause (e) of the incoming view result and $\varepsilon_f<1$ imply that the latter coefficient is nonzero on some valid encryption coins.
As $\varpi$ never vanishes on valid coins, the cleared comparison is a nonzero polynomial at fixed $r$.
The cleared guess-free term has degree at most $d_f$ by the incoming degree bound.
The cleared coefficients of linear guesses have degree at most $d_f$ because they are cleared constants or source-group values.
A pairing's product of two linear source expressions makes the coefficient of any quadratic guess monomial a field constant.
After clearing, such a coefficient has degree at most five because $\varpi$ has five linear factors.
The total degree bound is therefore $\max(d_f,d_f+1,7)=d_f+1$.
The grid polynomial bound with uniform guess values and valid encryption coins gives coincidence probability at most $(d_f+1)/(q-D)$.
This is at most $\varepsilon_f$ by its definition.

For a comparison with no guess variable in a source group, the incoming coincidence bound gives probability at most $\varepsilon_f$.
For one in $\mathbb G_T$, the incoming bound gives the same probability over encryption coins at any $r$ where the asserted equality is not an identity.
A comparison of distinct symbolic entries is nonformal by the symbolic game's entry rule.
A key comparison to $\kappa$ is nonformal by the incoming bound.
For an identity to give a bad event, the mark stack must be light because it is nonzero by the incoming demand.
All such $r$ lie in a single fiber of that stack by the incoming identity-locus demand.
This fiber has probability at most $\theta$ by lightness.
The total probability of a bad event for a comparison without guesses is therefore at most $\theta+\varepsilon_f$.

There are at most $L+3Q$ entries because each call has at most two operands and one result.
This bounds the number of comparison pairs and key tests involving guesses by $\binom{L+3u}{2}+L+3u$ since $Q\le u$.
For a collision without guesses at call $j$, the later entry is a result since a fresh guess could not cancel.
Its earlier partner is one of at most $L+3j-1$ entries.
A key test without guesses involves one of the at most $Q$ results or the two received target-group elements.
Summing the result-pair and key-test counts gives at most $QL+3Q(Q+1)/2+2$ non-guess comparisons that can account for a charged first mark.
This count is at most $N_{\mathrm{cmp}}(u)$ by substitution of $u=2Q+2$.
The union bound using these two comparison counts yields the claimed charged-mark probability.

add.label: Witness in low rank
add.name: Witness from a nonzero usable stack of rank at most three
add.statement: Write $\mathcal V$ for the stack's row space, $d=\dim\mathcal V$ and $K=\mathbb F_{q^n}$. For a matrix $B$ with columns a basis of $\mathcal V$ over $\mathbb F_q$, let $u_j$ be the transpose of row $j$ of $B$ and $h_s=B^\top\sigma^s(z)$, where $z$ is the coefficient vector of the form. Set $a=n/2-1$, $b=n/2$, and $c=n/2+1$. If the stack is nonzero and usable, $d\le3$, and $\mathcal V$ contains no kernel vector, then $\mathcal V$ contains a witness of $S$.
add.explain: Use the three tied matrix slices to isolate the witnesses in a Boolean cube inside the row space.
add.proof:
The nonzero stack has $d\ge1$.
The coordinates of $h_0$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb F_q$ because a dependence would give a kernel vector in the row space.
Frobenius carries that independence to $h_a=\sigma^a(h_0)$.
The Moore determinant of the first $d$ consecutive conjugates of $h_a$ is nonzero by the determinant demand.
Thus $h_a,h_b,h_c$ span $K^d$.
Index the three tied matrices by $W_a=W_U$, $W_b=W_V$ and $W_c=\sigma^c(W_U)$.
Choose a left inverse $E$ of $B$ over $\mathbb F_q$.
Define $M_s=EW_sE^\top$ for $s\in\{a,b,c\}$.
The column and row spaces of $W_s$ are contained in the scalar extension of the row space of the stack, because $W_s$ is a linear combination of symmetric cells.
Applying $BE$ on the left and its transpose on the right gives $W_s=BM_sB^\top$ because $BE$ projects onto the column span of $B$.
Each $W_s$ passes the linear tests over $K$ by linearity in the cells.
The ties give $M_s h_t=M_t h_s$ by injectivity of $B$.
The ties imply $(\sum_s e_s M_s)h_t=0$ for every $t\in\{a,b,c\}$ whenever $\sum_s e_s h_s=0$ with $e_s\in K$.
Since the $h_t$ span, this yields $\sum_s e_s M_s=0$.
There is therefore a linear map $h\mapsto M(h)$ with $M(h_s)=M_s$.
Define $T(h,x,y)=x^\top M(h)y$.
The form $T$ is symmetric in $x,y$ because $EW_sE^\top$ is symmetric for each $s$.
The ties extend by bilinearity to symmetry in $h,y$.
These two transpositions make $T$ symmetric.
Booleanity of the $W_s$ gives $T(h_s,u_j,u_j-u_0)=0$ for $j\in[N]$.
Since the $h_s$ span, $T(h,u_j,u_j-u_0)=0$ for all $h$.
The identity $a+c=n$ gives $M_a=\sigma^a(M_c)$ by the matrix definitions.
The even powers in $W_V$ give $M_b=\sigma^b(M_b)$.
When $u_0=0$, take a basis $l_1,\ldots,l_d$ from the remaining rows $u_j$.
Booleanity and symmetry imply that each $T(l_i,l_j,l_k)$ with a repeated index is zero.
If $d<3$, this forces $T=0$.
If $d=3$, the form is determined by its one all-distinct entry $e=T(l_1,l_2,l_3)$.
In that basis the off-diagonal entries of the bilinear form $T(h,\cdot,\cdot)$ are $e$ times the coordinates of $h$ at the corresponding missing indices.
The identities for $M_a,M_b$ therefore give $e h_s=\sigma^s(e)h_0$ for $s=a,b$.
If $e\ne 0$, then $h_a$ and $h_b$ belong to the line through $h_0$.
Independence of the three spanning vectors when $d=3$ excludes $e\ne0$.
Thus $T=0$ also when $d=3$.
The zero form would force every cell to vanish from the factorizations of $W_a,W_b$.
Therefore $u_0\ne0$.
Extend $l_0=u_0$ to a basis $l_0,l_1,\ldots,l_{d-1}$ of rows $u_j$.
For $\delta\in\{0,1\}^{d-1}$ let $p_\delta$ have coordinates $(1,\delta)$ in the basis dual to $(l_0,\ldots,l_{d-1})$.
Put $w_\delta=Bp_\delta$.
The relations $T(h,l_i,l_i)=T(h,l_i,l_0)$ for $i>0$ make the value of a basis triple depend only on its set of distinct nonzero indices.
The basis-triple entries of $\langle h,p_\delta\rangle\langle x,p_\delta\rangle\langle y,p_\delta\rangle$ are the Boolean monomials indexed by those sets.
The evaluation matrix with one row per subset is invertible because the square-free monomials form a basis of functions on the Boolean cube.
Consequently $M(h)=\sum_\delta C_\delta\langle h,p_\delta\rangle p_\delta p_\delta^\top$ for coefficients $C_\delta\in K$.
The same evaluation matrix on pairs of basis vectors shows that the squares $p_\delta p_\delta^\top$ are independent, since every subset of $[d-1]$ has size at most two.
Put $x_\delta=\langle h_0,p_\delta\rangle$, which is nonzero by independence of the coordinates of $h_0$.
Comparing the square coefficients in the Frobenius identities gives $C_\delta\sigma^s(x_\delta)=\sigma^s(C_\delta)x_\delta$ for $s=a,b$.
Hence $C_\delta/x_\delta$ is fixed by both $\sigma^a$ and $\sigma^b$.
The two powers differ by one, so $C_\delta/x_\delta$ is fixed by $\sigma$.
Thus write $C_\delta=\chi_\delta x_\delta$ with $\chi_\delta\in\mathbb F_q$.
Let $L$ be any linear test of $S$ over $\mathbb F_q$.
Applying $L$ to the displayed decomposition at each $h_s$ yields $h_0^\top Q_L h_s=0$ for $s=a,b,c$, where $Q_L=\sum_\delta\chi_\delta L(w_\delta w_\delta^\top)p_\delta p_\delta^\top$.
The spanning property gives $h_0^\top Q_L=0$.
The matrix $Q_L$ has entries in $\mathbb F_q$.
The independence of the coordinates of $h_0$ gives $Q_L=0$.
The independence of the squares gives $\chi_\delta L(w_\delta w_\delta^\top)=0$ for every $\delta$.
Since the stack is nonzero at least one $\chi_\delta$ is nonzero.
For such a $\delta$, $w_\delta$ has coordinate zero equal to $1$ by its definition in the dual basis.
Since $L$ was arbitrary, the moment matrix of this assignment passes all tests.
The test definitions therefore make $w_\delta$ a witness.

add.label: Asymptotic reduction time
add.name: Operation count for both reductions
add.statement: Under the hypotheses of the extraction theorem, if the adversary takes time $t$, makes at most $Q$ generic group calls, and makes at most $Q_H$ queries to each random oracle, both reductions $\mathcal B_0,\mathcal B_1$ take time at most $t_R=t+O(Q+d_R Q_H+\mu)+\operatorname{poly}(D,\log q)$ in the operation model of (R1)–(R5).
add.explain: Keep only the asymptotic overhead used by the extraction-error corollary.
add.proof:
Sample the seven points of (R2) at the beginning using the incoming invariance under sampling them early.
The private and recovery points need $O(N+1)$ independent coordinate samples each from the indicated finite sets.
The public polynomials need $O((N+1)D)$ coefficients because there are $2(N+1)$ interpolation polynomials and three extra polynomials of degree at most $D$.
The number of field coefficients of $M$ is $k(\ell+1)d_R$, polynomial in $D$ since $N<D$ and $(k+1)d_R=n\le D$.
The challenge entries and fresh seed are installed with one write per coefficient or oracle table entry, so (R1) programs its initial queries in time polynomial in $D$.
The forms of $M$ can be computed in polynomial time by multiplying its ring entries by the coordinate monomials and reducing modulo the defining polynomial of $R_q$.
The sampler draws at most $N+1$ independent search coordinates and obtains $r_0$ with $O(N)$ integer operations.
The published exponent count is polynomial in $D$ because each index in the encryption formulas ranges over at most $2D+1$ values by (P1) and the chunk definitions.
Each published exponent at any one point can be evaluated in polynomial time from the formulas, using polynomial evaluation and repeated field arithmetic.
The cost of assigning the initial labels is polynomial in $D$ because the model charges each table lookup, fresh sample and insertion as one operation.
Applying the stored key-oracle answer to the message in string-sized XOR blocks costs $O(\mu)$ operations.
Use one table from exponents to labels and another from examined strings to exponents or rejection for each group.
Maintain each table's entry count with its insertions.
At a previously unexamined operand string, uniformity of the remaining injection gives validity probability $(q-a)/u$ for $a$ assigned exponents and $u$ unexamined strings.
Implement the decision with one uniform sample from the interval specified by endpoints $0,u-1$ after the generators have labels and one comparison with $q-a$.
For a new valid operand, sample its exponent uniformly from unused exponents.
For a result with an unassigned exponent, sample its label uniformly from unexamined strings.
Each generic call makes at most two operand examinations and at most one result assignment, including the negative for a name request.
A flag on each target-group label records its eligibility for name requests, with one update when supplied initially or returned by addition, scalar multiplication or pairing.
The specified group formulas use a constant number of field operations on the exponents per call.
The expression record of a result needs one arithmetic node pointing to its at most two operand records, using the constant zero node for any missing record.
The private test maintains one field value per record with the same arithmetic on the private point's operand values.
The discrepancy test makes one comparison on the private values at each target-group result.
At the first mismatch retain pointers to the two records in the comparison.
The target record is available by a lookup of the target label from the masking step.
The table costs, record updates and discrepancy tests therefore give $O(Q)$ total overhead during group calls.
A lazy seed-oracle entry costs $O(d_R)$ operations for its coefficient samples and table access.
A lazy key-oracle entry costs a constant number of operations using a uniform sample from its finite output set $\{0,1\}^\mu$ and a table entry holding a reference to that sampled answer.
The random-oracle overhead during the run is therefore $O(d_R Q_H)$.
The circuit for a selected expression has at most one non-input node per generic call plus one final subtraction.
The exponents that depend on $r$ are right-leg inputs and their alpha copies.
At each recovery point, freeze the right-leg inputs of the other sector at their values there to select only the chosen sector's contribution to the derivative.
The incoming differentiation bound gives $O(Q)$ arithmetic for the circuit's derivatives with respect to its inputs at the point, apart from the polynomial-size initial input data.
The chain rule maps those input derivatives to the $r$ gradient by multiplying by the Jacobian of the explicit affine input exponents, a matrix with polynomially many entries in $D$.
There are only six recovery points per expression, so the total differentiation cost is $O(Q)+\operatorname{poly}(D,\log q)$.
Intersecting the span of the recovered vectors with the common kernel of the $n$ forms is a linear system with dimensions polynomial in $D$.
Packing a lifted vector is polynomial in $D$ and $\log q$ by its coordinate description.
There are at most two lift calls, whose time is polynomial in $D$ and $\log q$ by the incoming lift bound and $N<D$.
The additional code and embedded polynomial data have size polynomial in $D$ and $\log q$, plus $O(\mu)$ for the chosen message.
Adding the overheads to $t$ gives $t_R$.

add.label: View residue identities
add.name: View identities by residue and homogeneous components
add.statement:
Let $\mathsf{D}$ be an expression of $\mathbb{G}_T$, $\chi \in \mathbb{F}_q$, and $r, r' \in \mathbb{F}_q^{N+1}$.

 
(a) \emph{Passing stacks.} If $\mathsf{D}$ is $\chi\kappa$ identically at $r$, then in each sector $\mathsf{s}$ the stack $\mathbf{W}^{\mathsf{s}}(\mathsf{D})$ passes and satisfies the ties, $W^{\mathsf{s}}_c(\mathsf{D})\, r = u^{\mathsf{s}}_c(\mathsf{D})$ for every cell $c$, and the corner $\bigl( W^{\mathrm{plain}}_{c_{\mathrm{key}}}(\mathsf{D}) \bigr)_{00}$ is $\chi$.
(b) \emph{Locus.} If $\mathsf{D}$ is $\chi\kappa$ identically at $r$ and $W^{\mathsf{s}}_c(\mathsf{D})\, r' = u^{\mathsf{s}}_c(\mathsf{D})$ for every sector and cell, then $\mathsf{D}$ is $\chi\kappa$ identically at $r'$. In particular, if $\mathsf{D}$ is $\chi\kappa$ identically at $r$ and has zero stacks, then $\mathsf{D}$ is $\chi\kappa$ formally, and $\chi = 0$.
(c) \emph{Coincidence.} If $\mathsf{D}$ is not $\chi\kappa$ identically at $r$, $\Pr[\operatorname{val}(\mathsf{D}; \mathbf{c}, r) = \chi\kappa] \le d_f/(q - D) \le \varepsilon_f$ for uniform valid $\mathbf{c}$.
(d) \emph{No formal key scalar.} If $\chi \ne 0$, then $\mathsf{D}$ is not $\chi\kappa$ formally.
(e) \emph{Source groups.} If $\mathsf{E}$ and $\mathsf{E}'$ are expressions of $\mathbb{G}_1$, or of $\mathbb{G}_2$, that are not formally equal, then for every $r$ their values at $(\mathbf{c}, r)$ are equal with probability at most $\varepsilon_f$ over $\mathbf{c}$.

At any fixed-$r$ identity in (a), every coefficient on a second input $(\mathsf H^{\mathrm{leg}}_{j,1})^{\mathsf s}$ is zero except for a first input $\mathsf F^{k_1}_{i,1}$. That coefficient equals the one on the matching second coordinates $\mathsf F^{k_1}_{i,2}$ and $(\mathsf H^{\mathrm{leg}}_{j,2})^{\mathsf s}$. The monomial $s_{\mathrm X}\upsilon^{k_c}y_i$ determines the cell $c$ and row $i$. Formally equal target expressions have equal stacks and sketches. Two received elements of one group with formally unequal expressions collide with probability at most $\varepsilon_f$.

Write $\varpi=\Omega_{22}\zeta\zeta'\zeta''\varepsilon$ and $d_f=3D+2n+2K_1+6$. Write $x=\Omega_{12}$ and $b=\Omega_{22}$. In a fixed sector omit its superscript from $W_c$ and $u_c$. Write $\bar a$ for the exponent of a first input $a$ specialized at $b=0$. For $m=1,2$, define $L_{\mathrm{leg},j,\mathsf s}^m=\sum_{a\in\mathcal X_1} \mathsf D_{a,(\mathsf H^{\mathrm{leg}}_{j,m})^{\mathsf s}}\bar a$. Put $G_{\mathrm{leg},j,\mathsf s}=L_{\mathrm{leg},j,\mathsf s}^2-x L_{\mathrm{leg},j,\mathsf s}^1$.
add.proof:
At fixed $r$, the incoming degree bound makes $F=\varpi(\operatorname{val}(\mathsf D;\mathbf c,r)-\chi\kappa)$ a polynomial of degree at most $d_f$.
All factors of $\varpi$ are nonzero on the valid grid by their sampling sets.
The polynomial coincidence bound gives probability at most $d_f/(q-D)\le\varepsilon_f$ when the equality is not an identity at $r$.
An identity on the whole valid grid gives $F=0$ as a polynomial because $d_f/(q-D)<1$.
Dividing by the nonzero $\varpi$ gives the identity of exponents in the rational function field of the coins.
The only second-input exponents with a pole in $b$ are the right-leg factors.
Their Laurent coefficient of $b^{-1}$ in the identity is $\sum_{\mathrm{leg},j,\mathsf s}\alpha_{\mathsf s}s_{\mathrm{leg}}(B_j(\tau)-y_j)G_{\mathrm{leg},j,\mathsf s}=0$.
For fixed $j_0$, the coefficient of $t$ at $y=B(\tau)+t e_{j_0}$ is $-\sum_{\mathrm{leg},\mathsf s}\alpha_{\mathsf s}s_{\mathrm{leg}}G_{\mathrm{leg},j_0,\mathsf s}|_{y=B(\tau)}=0$.
The resulting equality for each sector is $\sum_{\mathrm{leg}}s_{\mathrm{leg}}G_{\mathrm{leg},j_0,\mathsf s}|_{y=B(\tau)}=0$, by comparing the two powers of $\alpha$.
At $b=0$, the exponent of each second left coordinate equals $x$ times its first-coordinate exponent.
The other first-input exponents at $b=0$ do not involve $x$.
The $B_i(\tau)$ are linearly independent by evaluating at the points $d_i$.
The classes of $1,\zeta\tau^k,\zeta'\tau^k,\zeta''B_i$ and $\pi_{k_1}B_i$ are distinct in $\zeta,\zeta',\zeta'',\pi$.
In non-$\pi$ classes the factors $s_{\mathrm{leg}}=s_{\mathrm X}\upsilon^{k_{\mathrm{leg}}}$ distinguish the legs.
The map $(c,i)\mapsto s_{\mathrm X}\upsilon^{k_c}y_i$ is injective by the cell exponent grid and the indeterminate indices.
Within each such class and leg or cell, the remaining factors are independent powers of $\tau$ or independent $B_i$.
For first inputs other than the $\mathsf F_{i,2}^{k_1}$, the specialized products $s_{\mathrm{leg}}\bar a|_{y=B(\tau)}$ are linearly independent in $a,\mathrm{leg}$.
The coefficient of $x^2$ therefore kills the pair coefficients of second left coordinates with first right coordinates.
The coefficient of $x$ now sets each first-right coefficient to its matching second-right coefficient for first left inputs, and to zero for all other first inputs.
In each sector let $\chi_{\mathrm{plain}}=\chi$ and $\chi_\alpha=-\mathsf D_K$.
The sector's part of class $\pi$ has value $\alpha_{\mathsf s}\chi_{\mathsf s}\kappa$ by the rational identity.
The class of a product leaves only matched left-right factors, first left factors with search bases or $G_2$, and power elements with the corresponding quotient, remainder or cancellation bases.
Matched coefficients make each paired left-right contribution proportional to the unmasked product $F^{k_1}_i H^{\mathrm{leg}}_j$ by the inverse basis matrices.
Collect the quotient powers at each cell into a polynomial $h_c$.
The remainder powers at a cell give an allowed polynomial $R_c$, since their exponents are $k+j\Delta'$ with $\nu\nmid k$ and $\nu\mid\Delta'$.
Using the factor-product table, the cell terms involving the leg scalars after removing $\alpha_{\mathsf s}$ are $\sum_c\gamma_c b_c$, where $b_c=y^\top(W_cr-u_c)+y^\top(W_c-W_c^\top)A(\tau)+(P_{W_c}+h_cZ_c+Z_0R_c)(\tau)$.
The displayed $b_c$ have no dependence on $s_{\mathrm X}$, $\upsilon$ or $\varepsilon$.
In $\sum_c\gamma_cb_c+\Phi=\chi_{\mathsf s}\kappa$, the remaining term $\Phi$ has no $s_{\mathrm X}$ by the mask, cancellation-base and generator formulas.
The distinct $\varepsilon$-free cell monomials give $b_{c_{\mathrm{key}}}=\chi_{\mathsf s}L_\rho$ and $b_c=0$ on all other cells.
Substitution of these identities makes $\Phi=0$.
The coefficient of $y$ in each cell identity is $W_cr-u_c+(W_c-W_c^\top)A(\tau)=0$.
Evaluating at $d_0$ gives $W_cr=u_c$.
The tabulated QAP vectors $A(p)$ for $p\in\{\rho,d_1,\ldots,d_N\}$ span the full space.
Thus $(W_c-W_c^\top)A(\tau)=0$ identically forces symmetry.
The constant-in-$y$ identity at $\rho$ in the key cell gives $(W_c)_{00}=\chi_{\mathsf s}$.
The degree of the quotient in each constant-in-$y$ identity is at most $2D-2-\deg Z_c$, by the degrees of the other terms.
The incoming QAP converse, with quotients $-h_c$ and remainders $-R_c$, therefore makes every $W_c$ pass.
By the mask identity and the tie bases, the coefficient of $\pi\eta_a\varepsilon^0$ in $\Phi$ is $y^\top(t_a(\upsilon)+P(\upsilon)Q_a(\upsilon))$ for a polynomial vector $Q_a$.
Its vanishing implies $P(T)\mid t_a(T)$ by comparison of the coordinates of $y$.
The hidden-basis support gives the difference when substituting $r'$ for $r$ as $\sum_{\mathsf s,c}\alpha_{\mathsf s}\gamma_c y^\top W_c^{\mathsf s}(r'-r)$.
This vanishes if $W_c^{\mathsf s}r'=u_c^{\mathsf s}$ for all sectors and cells.
If both stacks are zero, all $u_c^{\mathsf s}$ are zero by $W_cr=u_c$.
By the locus claim the equality is formal because the condition now holds for every $r'$.
For a formal equality to $\chi\kappa$, the equation $W_cr=u_c$ for every $r$ forces every $W_c$ to vanish.
The proved plain-key corner identity now gives $\chi=0$.
Formal equality of two target expressions therefore gives equal stacks by applying this result to their difference.
The corresponding probe sums agree because their cell matrices agree.
Pair a source-group difference with the opposite generator to preserve its exponent.
This target expression has zero stacks because the generator is outside every cell pair.
If these expressions are formally unequal, this target expression cannot be identically zero at any $r$ by the zero-stack conclusion.
The fixed-$r$ coincidence bound now applies to that pair.
For the two received target-group elements, injectivity of labels makes a collision equivalent to $1=\alpha\kappa$.
The conditional probability given $\kappa$ is at most $1/(q-1)$ by uniformity of the independent nonzero $\alpha$.
Averaging over $\kappa$ gives a collision probability at most $\varepsilon_f$, since $1/(q-1)\le\varepsilon_f$.
add.explain: Compare the full simple-pole coefficient before the homogeneous cell extraction and include the hidden-basis support in the statement.

edges.demand: For a nonidentically zero target-group comparison at fixed r, or a formally unequal source-group pair, coincidence over valid coins has probability at most ε_f. No expression equals κ formally. An identity in a nonformal target comparison prescribes one fiber of the nonzero mark stack.
After clearing by ϖ, a target expression minus χκ and a difference of source-group values are polynomials of total degree at most d_f.
